CTET Exam Date 2026 — Paper 1 & 2 Schedule, Shift Timings, Official Notification

CTET Exam Date 2026 has been officially announced by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). The 22nd edition of the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET) will be conducted on 6 September 2026 (Sunday) in offline (pen-and-paper) mode across various examination centres. Paper 2 (for Classes VI–VIII) will be held in the morning shift from 9:30 AM to 12:00 Noon, while Paper 1 (for Classes I–V) will take place in the afternoon shift from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM. The notification was released on 11 May 2026 at the official website ctet.nic.in.

📋 CTET Eligibility Criteria 2026 — Age Limit & Educational Qualification

The minimum age to apply for CTET 2026 is 18 years. There is no upper age limit for appearing in the CTET exam. Candidates from all age groups can apply unlimited times.

💻 How to Apply Online for CTET 2026

📘 Step-by-Step Application Process
  1. Visit Official Website: Go to ctet.nic.in
  2. Find Apply Link: Click on "CTET Apply Online" or "New Registration" on the homepage.
  3. Register: Fill in basic details to generate your application number and password.
  4. Log In: Use the credentials to access the CTET application form.
  5. Fill Details: Enter personal, academic, and exam preference details (Paper 1, Paper 2, or both).
  6. Upload Documents: Upload scanned photograph (3.5 cm x 4.5 cm, 10–100 KB, JPG/JPEG) and signature (3.5 cm x 1.5 cm, 3–30 KB, JPG/JPEG).
  7. Pay Fee: Pay the application fee online via Credit Card, Debit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  8. Submit & Print: Submit the form and download the confirmation page for future reference.
⚠️ Important Dates
  • Notification Release: 11 May 2026
  • Application Start: 11 May 2026
  • Last Date to Apply: 10 June 2026
  • Exam Date: 6 September 2026
  • Admit Card Release: A few weeks before the exam (likely August 2026)
  • Result Declaration: Last week of October 2026 (expected)

📝 CTET Selection Process & Certificate Validity

CTET Selection Flow
📝 Written Examination (Paper 1 or Paper 2) ↓ 📊 Qualifying Marks (60% General / 55% Reserved) ↓ 📜 CTET Certificate (Lifetime Validity) ↓ 💼 Apply for Teaching Jobs
📘 Selection Stages
  1. Written Examination: Candidates appear for Paper 1 (Classes I–V) or Paper 2 (Classes VI–VIII) or both. Each paper has 150 MCQs for 150 marks.
  2. Qualifying Marks: General category candidates must score 60% (90/150 marks); reserved category candidates (SC/ST/OBC/PwD) need 55% (82/150 marks).
  3. CTET Certificate: Successful candidates are issued a CTET certificate, which is now valid for a lifetime.
  4. Job Application: The CTET certificate is an eligibility criterion for teaching positions in central government schools (KVS, NVS, etc.) and many state schools.
🎓 Important — Certificate Validity
The CTET certificate is now valid for a lifetime (previously it was valid for only 7 years). This change was introduced by the NCTE in 2021. Qualified candidates can use their CTET certificate at any point in their career to apply for teaching vacancies.

CTET questions are based on NCERT syllabus for Classes I–V (Paper 1) and VI–VIII (Paper 2). However, the difficulty level can be up to secondary/senior secondary level for some subjects.

📚 CTET Syllabus 2026 — Paper 1 & 2

📘 CTET Paper 1 Syllabus (Classes I–V)
  • Child Development & Pedagogy: Educational psychology, learning theories, child development (6–11 years), inclusive education, assessment.
  • Language I: Comprehension, grammar, language pedagogy (chosen language).
  • Language II: Comprehension, grammar, language pedagogy (chosen language — different from Language I).
  • Mathematics: Number system, arithmetic, geometry, mensuration, data handling, math pedagogy.
  • Environmental Studies (EVS): Family, food, shelter, water, travel, things we make and do, EVS pedagogy.
📘 CTET Paper 2 Syllabus (Classes VI–VIII)
  • Child Development & Pedagogy: Educational psychology, learning theories, child development (11–14 years), inclusive education, assessment.
  • Language I: Comprehension, grammar, language pedagogy (chosen language).
  • Language II: Comprehension, grammar, language pedagogy (chosen language — different from Language I).
  • Mathematics & Science (Option A): Mathematics (number systems, algebra, geometry, mensuration, data handling) + Science (physics, chemistry, biology).
  • Social Studies / Social Science (Option B): History, Geography, Political Science, Economics, and Social Studies pedagogy.

💰 CTET Salary Structure 2026 — PRT, TGT & PGT Pay Scale

💡 Additional Allowances
In addition to the basic pay, government teachers receive Dearness Allowance (DA) (currently ~46%), House Rent Allowance (HRA) (up to 24%), Medical Allowance, NPS pension, and Leave Travel Concession (LTC).

🎓 PHD Teacher Insight — Exam Strategy
While the qualifying marks are 60% (General) and 55% (Reserved), scoring 110–130 marks gives you a stronger edge in the job market. Many KVS and NVS recruitment processes give weightage to CTET scores. Focus on Child Development & Pedagogy and Language I & II — these sections carry 90 marks combined and are often the differentiator.

  • 2025 (Expected): General 88–90, Reserved 82–87

❓ Frequently Asked Questions — CTET Exam Date 2026

1. What is the CTET Exam Date 2026?

The CTET Exam Date 2026 is 6 September 2026 (Sunday). The exam will be conducted in offline mode across India.

2. What are the shift timings for CTET 2026?

Paper 2 (Classes VI–VIII) will be held in the morning shift from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM. Paper 1 (Classes I–V) will be held in the afternoon shift from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM.

3. What is the age limit for CTET 2026?

The minimum age to apply for CTET 2026 is 18 years. There is no upper age limit. Candidates can appear unlimited times.

4. What is the educational qualification for CTET Paper 1?

For CTET Paper 1 (Classes I–V), candidates must have Senior Secondary (12th) with 50% marks + 2-year D.El.Ed (or equivalent as per NCTE norms).

5. What is the educational qualification for CTET Paper 2?

For CTET Paper 2 (Classes VI–VIII), candidates must have Graduation with 50% marks + 1-year B.Ed (or equivalent as per NCTE norms).

6. Is there negative marking in CTET 2026?

No, there is no negative marking in the CTET exam. Candidates are awarded 1 mark for each correct answer, and there is no penalty for incorrect answers.

7. What are the qualifying marks for CTET 2026?

General category candidates need 60% (90/150 marks). Reserved category candidates (SC/ST/OBC/PwD) need 55% (82/150 marks).

8. How long is the CTET certificate valid?

The CTET certificate is now valid for a lifetime. Earlier it was valid for only 7 years.

9. What is the application fee for CTET 2026?

For General/OBC candidates: ₹1,000 for one paper, ₹1,200 for both papers. For SC/ST/PwD candidates: ₹500 for one paper, ₹600 for both papers.

10. Where can I download the CTET Notification 2026 PDF?

You can download the official CTET Notification 2026 PDF from the CTET official website: ctet.nic.in → Public Notices / Information Bulletin section.
